thread:
jane_acme: Hey team — we're seeing truncated streaming responses from the Redwood API when our client reconnects. The final JSON object is cut off and there is no finish_reason field. Happened multiple times in the last hour. Request-id: rq_6a2f9b. Repro steps below.

alex_support: Thanks Jane — sorry about that. Can you paste the raw response you get from the streaming endpoint (curl okay) and confirm whether you used any proxy or CDN in front of you? Also include the exact Authorization header format (no token value needed).

jane_acme: Repro curl we used:```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-3b'
```Partial output (we saw it stop mid-object):```event: message
data: {"id":"tok_abc","text":"Here is the answer so far", "meta": {
...lots of tokens...
"chunk_id": 45,
"partial": true}

event: message
data: {"id":"tok_abc","text":"continuing..."}

// connection drops, client reconnects
// on reconnect we requested resume with last_seq=45
// final chunk expected but client receives:
{\"id\":\"tok_abc\",\"text\":\"final line\",\"meta\":{\"finish_reason\":}

// this is invalid JSON (finish_reason missing) and parse fails on our side
```We do have Fastly in front of the app and sometimes an internal gateway.

alex_support: Got it. We're going to escalate. For now, can you attach the full curl output saved to a file (including raw bytes) and the exact headers your client sends on the reconnect? That will help trace whether bytes are dropped pre-Redwood or in our runtime. I'll also open a ticket with eng-runtime & eng-sre.

deploy_bot: Deploy notice: edge/proxy routing change deployed by infra at 1749968900 — toggled chunked-encoding buffering flag for fast-path.

tim_sre: @alex_support @maria_engineer tagging SRE. The deploy change might be relevant — if the proxy coalesces or prematurely terminates an HTTP/2 stream it can drop final bytes. Jane, can you try a quick reproduce with `--no-buffer` and `--http1.1` flags to see whether the behavior is tied to http2/fastly buffering? Also please include `--trace-ascii` output if possible.

jane_acme: Tried `--http1.1 --no-buffer` and still hit the truncated final object, though fewer occurrences. Attached a 2MB raw capture from the client.

maria_engineer: Thanks for the captures — I've started looking. Preliminary notes: our rejoin/resume logic emits a final sentinel/event (we rely on `finish_reason`) but I see cases where the runtime emits the final bytes but Fastly's buffering combined with a reconnect race can drop the final chunk before the client sees it. On reconnect we attempt to synthesize a final event when resume fails, but there's a race where the serialized JSON can be truncated if we stream a small final frame that gets merged then cut by the CDN.

maria_engineer: Short-term mitigation we can recommend to customers: parse streams leniently (allow trailing commas/missing finish_reason) and fall back to polling the non-streaming endpoint for final full result when a resume returns incomplete JSON.

maria_engineer: Medium-term fix I'm proposing: 1) Add an explicit final SSE event `event: done\ndata: {\"_final\":true,\"finish_reason\":\"stop\"}` that we flush in its own chunk and ensure it's retried when reconnect/resume flags are present. 2) Add server-side idempotent re-emit for last-final-chunk when a resume-request indicates the client missed the terminal event.

alex_support: That sounds reasonable. From a support perspective, can we ship a config toggle for Private/Dedicated customers first, then a hotfix for hosted? Tim, is this something SRE can help QA with Fastly staging?

tim_sre: Yep, we can run a staged Fastly config that disables coalescing for SSE-like endpoints and verify the sentinel chunk reaches clients reliably. I'll coordinate a canary and add additional logging on the proxy to detect partial chunk drops.

jane_acme: Appreciate the plan. Any ETA for a hosted fix? The issue impacts a throttled production job; we can tolerate a manual poll workaround for now but would like a proper fix.

maria_engineer: If we greenlight a hotfix, we can patch the runtime to emit the new `event: done` sentinel and a defensive re-emit within ~48 hours, then run Fastly staging tests. Full rollout to hosted could be 72–96 hours if QA goes smoothly.

alex_support: Jane — do you want us to apply the poll-fallback guidance to your integration docs and add a short-term parsing tolerant patch on your client? We can also enable increased logging on your tenant to capture any further truncated streams.

jane_acme: Yes please — enable tenant debug logs and send the short-term parsing guidance. We'll add the tolerant parser and polling fallback today. Thanks for moving fast.

alex_support: Will do — I've escalated with ticket ENG-STREAM-4821 and assigned to @maria_engineer. We'll update this thread when the staging test passes or if we need a canary window scheduled. :thumbsup:

maria_engineer: One last note for engineers: if you see `finish_reason` omitted, treat it as equivalent to `\"finish_reason\": \"unknown_truncate\"` for metric tagging so we can aggregate these cases. We'll add a diagnostic field to the emitted final sentinel to help postmortem tracing.

jane_acme: Thanks everyone, looking forward to the follow-up.
__notes: do not include a title field per agents.md
